owner.name: Covenant Peace
owner.tagline: Low-latency systems & digital design — where C++ meets the FPGA
owner.summary: Engineer building toward the intersection of high-performance C++ and FPGA digital design, targeting roles in electronic trading and hardware acceleration. This portfolio tracks a structured, year-long progression from foundations to production-grade projects in both domains.

meta.goal: Build a job-ready portfolio across low-latency C++ and SystemVerilog/VHDL, culminating in FPGA-accelerated trading projects.
meta.cadenceNote: Target ~2 projects/month. Each project is 'done' only when it meets its level's Definition of Done (see docs/workflow.md).

levels.label: Foundation
levels.note: Core syntax, tooling, and single-concept exercises. Proof you can build, test, and explain the basics.

levels.label: Basic
levels.note: Small complete projects that solve a real, self-contained problem end to end.

levels.label: Medium
levels.note: Multi-component systems with real engineering trade-offs, tests, and measurements.

levels.label: Robust
levels.note: Production-grade work: benchmarked, verified, documented, and defensible in an interview.

tracks.label: C++ / Low-Latency
tracks.blurb: Modern C++ for trading, market data, and performance-critical systems.

tracks.label: SystemVerilog / VHDL
tracks.blurb: RTL design and verification, from logic fundamentals to a CPU core on real FPGA hardware.

tracks.label: HW/SW Co-Design
tracks.blurb: The headline story: C++ and FPGA working together for low-latency trading.

projects.title: Modern C++ Foundations & Data-Structure Katas
projects.summary: From-scratch ring buffer, static_vector, and intrusive doubly-linked list — allocation-conscious structures with self-checking tests and complexity notes.
projects.whyItMatters: Interviewers probe ownership, RAII, move semantics, and cache-aware data layout. These katas are where you earn the vocabulary.

projects.title: Market-Data CSV/Tick Parser & Stats Engine
projects.summary: Parse a historical tick/OHLCV file into typed records, compute rolling stats (VWAP, min/max, returns), and stream results. Zero-copy parsing where possible.
projects.whyItMatters: Every trading system starts with ingesting and normalizing market data fast. Shows you can handle real financial data formats.

projects.title: Limit Order Book
projects.summary: A price-time-priority order book supporting add/cancel/modify and top-of-book queries, with a clean API and a replay test harness driven by a recorded order stream.
projects.whyItMatters: The order book is THE canonical trading interview project. A correct, well-tested one is a strong signal on its own.

projects.title: Moving-Average Strategy Backtester
projects.summary: An event-driven backtester for a simple MA-crossover strategy: feeds historical bars, simulates fills, tracks PnL, and reports Sharpe, drawdown, and a trade log.
projects.whyItMatters: Demonstrates you understand the simulation loop, fill logic, and performance metrics that quant roles live in.

projects.title: Price-Time Matching Engine
projects.summary: Extend the order book into a matching engine that generates trades and order-ack/fill events, with a deterministic replay mode and property-based tests on book invariants.
projects.whyItMatters: Matching engines sit at the core of every exchange and many trading sims. Deterministic, invariant-checked matching is senior-level signal.

projects.title: Lock-Free SPSC / MPMC Queues
projects.summary: Cache-line-aware single-producer/single-consumer and bounded multi-producer queues, with correctness tests under TSan and throughput/latency benchmarks vs std alternatives.
projects.whyItMatters: Low-latency pipelines live or die on the queues between threads. This is direct HFT infrastructure knowledge.

projects.title: Low-Latency Asynchronous Logger
projects.summary: A logging library that keeps the hot path near-zero-cost by deferring formatting to a background thread via a lock-free queue, with nanosecond-stamped records.
projects.whyItMatters: Shows you understand that observability must not cost latency — a real concern in trading systems.

projects.title: Exchange Feed Handler (ITCH-style)
projects.summary: Decode a binary, ITCH-style market-data protocol into normalized book updates, feeding the limit order book. Includes a synthetic feed generator and conformance tests.
projects.whyItMatters: Parsing a real binary exchange protocol into a live book is as close to production trading infrastructure as a portfolio project gets.

projects.title: Event-Driven Backtesting Framework
projects.summary: A reusable backtesting framework: pluggable strategies, realistic fill models (slippage, latency), portfolio accounting, and a reporting pipeline. Benchmarked on multi-year data.
projects.whyItMatters: A framework others could plug into shows architecture skill, not just a one-off script. Strong for quant-dev roles.

projects.title: Combinational Logic + Blinky on FPGA
projects.summary: Adders, muxes, and decoders in SystemVerilog with self-checking testbenches, plus a 'blinky'/LED + button design synthesized and run on your FPGA board.
projects.whyItMatters: Proves the full flow works end to end: write RTL, simulate, synthesize, and see it on real silicon.

projects.title: Sequential Logic: Counters, FSMs & Debouncer
projects.summary: Parameterized counters, a Moore/Mealy FSM (e.g. traffic light or sequence detector), and a button debouncer — each with waveform-verified testbenches.
projects.whyItMatters: Clocked logic and clean FSM coding style are the bread and butter every hardware interviewer checks.

projects.title: UART Transmitter / Receiver
projects.summary: A configurable-baud UART TX/RX with oversampling, FIFO buffering, and a loopback test on the board talking to your PC's serial terminal.
projects.whyItMatters: A classic, demonstrable peripheral — talking to a real serial terminal is a satisfying, interview-friendly demo.

projects.title: SPI & I2C Master Controllers
projects.summary: SPI and I2C master controllers driving a real on-board or external sensor/peripheral, with testbenches modeling the slave device.
projects.whyItMatters: Shows you can implement standard interface protocols to spec and verify them against a modeled slave.

projects.title: Synchronous & Asynchronous FIFO (CDC)
projects.summary: A sync FIFO and an async FIFO with Gray-code pointers for safe clock-domain crossing, with testbenches that stress near-full/near-empty and dual-clock scenarios.
projects.whyItMatters: Clock-domain crossing is where junior designs break. A correct async FIFO is a strong competence signal.

projects.title: Pipelined Fixed-Point FIR Filter
projects.summary: A parameterizable, pipelined FIR filter in fixed-point arithmetic, verified against a reference model (Python/C++) with quantization-error analysis and timing closure.
projects.whyItMatters: DSP + pipelining + fixed-point + timing closure is exactly the skill set for signal/trading datapath design.

projects.title: AXI-Lite / AXI-Stream Peripheral
projects.summary: A register-mapped AXI-Lite peripheral plus an AXI-Stream data path, integrated into a block design and driven from a soft-core or host, with protocol-compliance checks.
projects.whyItMatters: AXI is the lingua franca of FPGA SoC design. Showing clean AXI interfaces makes you immediately useful on real projects.

projects.title: Multi-Cycle RISC-V Core (RV32I)
projects.summary: A multi-cycle RV32I CPU that runs real compiled programs, verified instruction-by-instruction against a golden ISA model, and demonstrated on the FPGA.
projects.whyItMatters: Building a working CPU proves deep understanding of datapath, control, and verification — a flagship resume item.

projects.title: Pipelined RISC-V Core with Hazard Handling
projects.summary: A 5-stage pipelined RV32I core with forwarding, stalls, and branch handling, benchmarked on CoreMark-style workloads and verified against the golden model.
projects.whyItMatters: Pipelining and hazard resolution are the hard part of CPU design — this is the project that separates serious candidates.

projects.title: UVM Verification Environment
projects.summary: A UVM testbench for one of your DUTs (e.g. the FIFO or AXI peripheral): driver, monitor, scoreboard, coverage, and constrained-random tests reaching a coverage goal.
projects.whyItMatters: Verification is half of all hardware jobs. Real UVM with coverage closure is rare in a portfolio and highly valued.

projects.title: Hardware Top-of-Book Accelerator
projects.summary: An FPGA module that maintains top-of-book from a stream of order updates, compared against the C++ limit order book for correctness and measured for update latency.
projects.whyItMatters: The first concrete HW/SW co-design piece: the same problem solved in C++ and in hardware, with a latency comparison. Perfect interview narrative.

projects.title: FPGA Market-Data Parser + C++ Host Pipeline
projects.summary: A hardware parser that decodes an ITCH-style feed in the FPGA fabric and streams normalized updates to a C++ host app over UART/Ethernet, end-to-end latency measured.
projects.whyItMatters: This is the capstone: a line-rate hardware feed parser feeding software. It is exactly what FPGA-trading teams build.
